customManagers.description: The S3 server image the test containers pin in tests/Shared/S3Emulator.cs (ADR-0110). Grouped below with the same image in docker-compose.yml so the two move together.

The API Dockerfile pulls the Lambda Web Adapter from this org's GHCR mirror, never public.ecr.aws (#629). The tag and digest on that line are upstream's, so track them against upstream; tools/build/mirror-lambda-adapter.sh copies a bumped version on the next release.

packageRules.description: The GHCR mirror of the Lambda Web Adapter holds only the versions release.yml copied into it; the regex manager above tracks the same line against upstream instead (#629).
Label major updates as breaking changes

Approve and automerge non-major updates. platformAutomerge holds a PR until the REQUIRED status checks pass; the ruleset that makes them required (build, test, coverage, web, e2e, agent-config, i18n, linked-issue, lint, and the rest of the main ruleset) was confirmed live before this flag was flipped - see ADR-0011 and #35.

A web dependency PR changes src/web/package.json or its lock file, and feature-coverage counts src/** as behavior-bearing. The PR cites the Playwright-covered claims the bump leaves standing, in the one shape tools/spec/check-feature-coverage.ts accepts; the required web and e2e checks re-prove those claims on the same PR, and the dependency category fails if anything but a manifest or lock file changed (ADR-0090, ADR-0111).
prBodyNotes: No .feature scenario needed: dependency — a web package or lock version moved; no application source file changed
Claims preserved: REQ-SUB-001, REQ-SUB-029, REQ-SUB-045, REQ-MOD-003, REQ-MOD-052, REQ-QB-076

packageRules.description: The .NET SDK in global.json is pinned deliberately; never automerge it. Renovate reads global.json with its nuget manager as the dependency dotnet-sdk; there is no dotnet-sdk manager, so matching on one matched nothing (ADR-0120).

Hold the .NET SDK and every mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet image to the major the projects target. Renovate cannot see the target framework, so on its own it offered runtime:11.0 to a net10.0 Worker that would not start on it (#429). Digest, minor, and patch updates still flow. The next major is moved by hand in one pull request: global.json, <TargetFramework> in Directory.Build.props, the Dockerfile FROM, and this allowedVersions. tools/build/check-dotnet-major.ts fails the docs check when they disagree (ADR-0120).

tools/dev/act/Dockerfile's amd64 stage supplies the x86-64 loader and glibc for the act image, whose base is catthehacker's act-24.04 (ADR-0145). It stays on that release, so a local run loads amd64 downloads against the runner's glibc; #551 moved it to 26.04 alone (#552). Digest updates within 24.04 still flow. The next release moves both FROM lines by hand in one pull request.

A Worker base-image bump changes src/HpacSafety.Worker/Dockerfile, and feature-coverage counts src/** as behavior-bearing. The PR cites the video claims the image carries. The required build check re-proves them by building the image and running ffmpeg and ffprobe inside it. The dependency category fails if anything but a manifest, lock file, or Dockerfile changed (ADR-0090, ADR-0111, ADR-0120).
prBodyNotes: No .feature scenario needed: dependency — the Worker's base image moved within its .NET major; no application source file changed

packageRules.description: Renovate's terraform manager computes .terraform.lock.hcl checksums itself instead of running terraform, and has produced a checksum that did not match the registry's real package (issue #118). Disabled here; .github/workflows/terraform-relock.yml regenerates the lock file with the real terraform binary on a schedule instead, verified by the required infra CI check.
The coverage toolchain, matching its ItemGroup in Directory.Packages.props. reportgenerator lives in .config/dotnet-tools.json but belongs with the collector it consumes.

@vitejs/plugin-react's major version is peer-locked to vite's (6.x requires vite ^8.0.0) — a solo bump of either breaks npm's peer resolution (#119). Move them together, same reasoning as EntityFrameworkCore/Npgsql below.
EF Core and the Npgsql PROVIDER must move together or migrations break. The bare Npgsql driver is a different vendor on its own cadence and is grouped separately.
The bare Npgsql driver, matching its ItemGroup in Directory.Packages.props. Excludes the EF Core provider, which is pinned to EF Core's cadence above.
The development and test S3 server, pinned in docker-compose.yml and tests/Shared/S3Emulator.cs (ADR-0110). One pull request moves both.

ESLint and the plugins the root lint config loads move as one group. ESLint stays on a major until every plugin's peer range accepts the next one: until then npm ci cannot resolve the group's lock file, the required lint check fails, and the pull request cannot merge (#784, lesson 0042). A plugin release that widens its range lands first, and Renovate rebases the held pull request onto it; once it resolves and every required check passes, it automerges, major included (#789).
